title: MODAL-ORGANIZATIONAL THEORY OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
abstract: One of the fundamental problems in contemporary artificial intelligence research concerns the relationship between the computational structures of intelligent systems and the cognitive capabilities they exhibit. Although artificial neural networks are typically described in terms of computational units, parameters, architectures, internal representations, and information-processing mechanisms, these descriptions do not fully resolve the conceptual distinction between operations currently performed by a system, operations that remain accessible under specified conditions, and transformations that may alter the system's repertoire of possible cognitive activities.This treatise develops a modal-organizational framework for analyzing artificial intelligence through the structure of its functional possibilities, the constraints governing their realization, and the transformations through which these possibilities may change.The central argument is that the organization of an intelligent artificial system cannot be adequately characterized solely by its currently realized computations. A broader analysis must also account for the relations between available operations, the conditions governing their composition, the resources required for their realization, and the permissible transformations of the organizational structures themselves.The proposed framework distinguishes five analytical levels: physical implementation, computational structure, causal-functional organization, compositional organization, and the modal structure of cognitive capabilities.A formal model of cognitive organization is introduced in terms of states, operators, composition rules, organizational constraints, and resource costs. On this basis, three categories of cognitive possibility are distinguished: actualized, operationally accessible, and transformationally accessible capabilities.The treatise further differentiates four types of organizational change: behavioral variation, compositional expansion, organizational-rule reconfiguration, and representational-space transformation.Four elementary formal propositions are developed concerning the invariance of capabilities under structure-preserving recoding, the insufficiency of restricted behavioral equivalence for establishing modal equivalence, the conservativity of adding an already definable operator, and the dependence of resource-bounded capabilities on implementation costs.The framework is examined in relation to causal abstraction, mechanistic explanation, functionalism, multiple realizability, computational mechanics, category-theoretic compositionality, dynamical systems, and theories of transformational creativity.A central conclusion is that novelty of output, novelty of capability, novelty of mechanism, and novelty of organizational principle must be treated as conceptually distinct phenomena.The proposed theory does not claim to establish a new physical constituent of intelligence or an empirically verified universal mechanism. Its contribution is a systematic philosophical and formal framework for examining the relationship between computational realization, organizational structure, functional possibility, and transformations of the space of accessible cognitive operations.

title: Human-Centric Trustworthy AI: AITHENA’s Methodological Framework for CCAM and Key Insights
abstract: This paper presents AITHENA’s human-centric, trustworthy AI methodology tailored for Cooperative, Connected and Automated Mobility (CCAM) systems. Recognising that public trust is essential to the adoption of AI-powered mobility, the framework translates high-level ethical principles, i.e., fairness, transparency, accountability, and privacy, into a practical Trustworthy AI qualitative checklist for developers, operators, and regulators. By integrating empirical user research on user mobility needs, expectations, and concerns, the methodology offers concrete tools to address trust challenges regarding AI in CCAM. The paper details how user perspectives are mapped to actionable checklist items, outlines implementation guidance, and discusses policy pathways aligned with the EU AI Act and automotive safety standards. Ultimately, AITHENA aims to bridge the gap between ethical theory and real-world application, fostering AI-driven mobility systems that reflect societal values and regulatory requirements.

title: Identity in the Age of AI: Toward a Functional Postphenomenology
abstract: Advanced AI systems increasingly mediate the cognitive and practical functions through which personal identity is enacted: intention formation, deliberation, memory, self-expression, preference formation, and relational interaction. Drawing on Western and Confucian conceptions of identity, this paper advances a functional hypothesis specifying six domains in which AI may be reorganizing the conditions of agency, and outlines the implications for responsibility, consent, dignity, and institutional design. The argument is functional and normative rather than metaphysical: not that agency disappears, but that the architecture of the self that is presupposed by our normative categories may require renewed examination.

title: Model choice and prompt framing in LLM sustainability judgments
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for sustainability assessment and decision support, yet their judgments may depend on the selected model and on how the task is defined. We compare 13 locally executed open-weight LLMs on 80 author-written sustainability scenarios using three prompt families that ask which actor should be responsible, bear the costs, or initiate action. Each model answered at two temperature settings with 100 repetitions, producing 624,000 deposited outputs, of which 610,708 contain a complete score vector. Scores were analyzed as relative actor support after removing each response’s overall level. Within this instrument, the cost prompt family produced the highest cross-model disagreement, exceeding both responsibility and catalyst by 7.37 points (question-cluster 95% intervals 5.56−9.15 and 5.38−9.36, describing variation across these 80 scenarios). It also produced the most lead-actor disagreement and the lowest full consensus. Moving from catalyst to cost reduced relative support for government and increased it for individuals and firms; moving from cost to responsibility largely reversed this pattern. These differences exceeded temperature-setting differences and persisted under model exclusion, alternative score transformations and tie rules, missing-response checks, and stems without explicit cost wording. Exploratory category patterns are conditional on uneven item coverage. Secondary rationale-language comparisons show the same within-model ordering but not the most cross-model variation under cost. Operational use should disclose model, prompt, and temperature choices; compare plausible alternatives; repeat generations; and refer high-disagreement judgments for human deliberation.

title: When Strong Reasoners Join the Pool: Small Union Premiums and Costly Runaway Generations in LLM Routing
abstract: Routing benchmarks often judge a router against a hindsight oracle that counts a query as solved whenever any model's recorded answer is correct, but under stochastic decoding that oracle mixes two different objects: the clairvoyant ceiling of committing to one model per query and the premium of calling several models and keeping any correct answer. A companion study measured this premium at 3.5 percentage points (pp) for 11 small open models on MATH-500; how large it is once current reasoning models enter the pool was unknown. We measure it with a fixed-protocol, pre-committed generation on a single NVIDIA B300: all 500 MATH-500 problems, 30 seeded samples per problem, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and NVIDIA's Nemotron Nano 9B v2 and Nemotron Super 49B v1.5 (a NAS derivative of the same 70B) under vendor sampling, a 65,536-token cap, a pinned Math-Verify scorer, and an append-only attempt ledger, for 45,000 scored responses. The two reasoning models both reach 96.1% accuracy against 76.2% for the 70B baseline. The empirical product-coupling premium is 0.215-0.588 pp across all two- and three-model pools; the empirical plug-in selection headroom over always calling Nano is 1.27 pp; and resampling Nano three times gives practically the same empirical any-correct rate as calling all three models once. Only 31 responses reached the cap, 25 of them with exactly periodic tails, yet the capped responses account for up to 60.2% of a model's output-length-squared proxy, and long generations made a fourth planned model, Llama-3.1-8B, too slow to finish. The premium is far below the companion's 3.5 pp, but models, pool size and protocol changed together; an oracle gap should therefore be reported with the pool, the protocol, the samples per cell and the decoding budget that produced it.

title: Mytho-MoE: Knowledge Graph Datasets, Model Checkpoints, and Experimental Evidence
abstract: This record contains research artifacts for Mytho-MoE, a question-level mixture of domain-specific LoRA experts using a frozen Qwen3-4B backbone. The system includes independently trained Harivamsha (HVM) and Ramayana (RaMO) expert adapters, an original mixed-task router, and a router further adapted using graph-derived natural-language questions. The release provides author-constructed RDF knowledge graphs, instruction datasets, router-adaptation splits, evaluation questions and reference answers, saved predictions, aggregate results, model checkpoints, and a snapshot of the accompanying code. Dataset construction used English translations of the Harivamsha Purana and the Ramayana of Valmiki available through Wisdom Library, with AI assistance and manual review. Source URLs and construction details are documented in the accompanying files. The expert instruction datasets contain 200,248 accepted training records and 22,100 validation records. Evaluation cohorts overlap and should not be treated as independent samples. An audit identified 588 HVM validation rows with identical task, query, and target records in HVM training. The release documents this overlap and other evaluation limitations. Handwritten diagnostic questions were used during development. See the README and verification reports for file descriptions, checkpoint requirements, reproduction instructions, and limitations.

title: 可观察的定义(第二层):漂移、适应、维持(数字生命·草稿)
abstract: 可观察定义第二层。分段流、每段最优预测器、漂移 Δ_i(用上一段最优预测器预测新段多损失多少)、更新规则 U、适应代价;定义"维持":在阈值 τ、时长 T、代价预算 B_U 内,损失一直 ≤ τ;定义"可维持性"。本层"生命"最小定义 = 维持型系统:有持久状态、能按需更新、漂移下可维持、代价有界。观察性事实:漂移越大要的更新/代价越多;只优化当前段会遗忘旧段(回放缓解);跨段保留状态更省样本。可检验预测:漂移-代价曲线、更新频率-遗忘曲线、持久状态 vs 重置、固定预算下最优更新频率。对应原型:论文-56 的 noop/update 与旧内容重放就是本层定义的一个实例。

title: LFM2.5-24B-A2B
abstract: Preservation mirror. This Zenodo record is a long-term preservation mirror of the official Hugging Face repository LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B published by LiquidAI, mirrored byte-for-byte at the pinned revision 3dc4cd09c9a2a99e1e819693e79d3aba5e9bb4f2 (revision tree). The deposit contains the complete 27-file repository snapshot (47,964,603,149 bytes) exactly as published upstream — no file was modified, converted, quantized or re-sharded. An identical preservation copy is held at the Internet Archive: archive.org/details/liquidai-lfm2-5-24b-a2b-hf-preservation-2026-001. License: LFM Open License v1.0 — https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B/blob/3dc4cd09c9a2a99e1e819693e79d3aba5e9bb4f2/LICENSE. The original license terms as published by LiquidAI govern; where the repository contains a LICENSE file it is included among the deposited files. The publisher's own model card (LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B @ 3dc4cd09) follows, reproduced in full. Try LFM • Docs • Discord LFM2.5-24B-A2B LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a 24B-parameter reasoning model with only 2B active parameters, built for fast, private agents on-device. It is the largest and final model in the LFM2.5 family, which now spans two orders of magnitude: from LFM2.5-230M to LFM2.5-24B-A2B. Best-in-class agent: Competitive with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a model with ~50% more total and active parameters, on agentic and tool-use tasks, scoring 48.09 on LiveClaw versus 38.19. Reasoning at MoE speed: Always thinks before it answers. With only 2B active parameters per token, each reasoning token is cheap. Efficient inference: Runs up to 1.7× faster than comparable MoEs on-device, with 184 tok/s on an Apple M5 Max and up to 21K output tok/s on a single NVIDIA B300 GPU. Find more information about LFM2.5-24B-A2B in our blog post. 🗒️ Model Details Model Parameters Description LFM2.5-24B-A2B-Base 24B (2B active) Pre-trained base model for fine-tuning LFM2.5-24B-A2B 24B (2B active) Post-trained for agentic workloads LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a general-purpose text-only reasoning model with the following features: Total parameters: 24.0B Active parameters: 2.45B Number of layers: 40 (30 double-gated short convolution blocks + 10 GQA) Experts: 64 per MoE block, top-4 routing Training budget: 36 trillion tokens Vocabulary size: 128,000 Context length: 131,072 tokens Languages: English, Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish, Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian, Hindi, Russian, Polish Generation parameters: temperature: 0.1 top_k: 50 repetition_penalty: 1.05 Model Description LFM2.5-24B-A2B Original model checkpoint in native format. Best for fine-tuning or inference with Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang. LFM2.5-24B-A2B-FP8 FP8 checkpoint (block-wise FP8 weights, dynamic FP8 activations). Best for high-throughput GPU serving with vLLM and SGLang with lower memory usage. LFM2.5-24B-A2B-GGUF Quantized format for llama.cpp and compatible tools. Optimized for CPU inference and local deployment with reduced memory usage. LFM2.5-24B-A2B-ONNX ONNX Runtime format for cross-platform deployment. Enables hardware-accelerated inference across diverse environments (cloud, edge, mobile). LFM2.5-24B-A2B-MLX-4bit MLX format for Apple Silicon. Optimized for fast inference on Mac devices using the MLX framework. LFM2.5-24B-A2B-DSpark DSpark draft model for speculative decoding with SGLang, for faster generation. Coming soon. We recommend using it for agents that need to reason, call tools, and run reliably on your device. It is not recommended for knowledge-heavy tasks on its own: pair it with retrieval or web search, which plays to its tool-calling strength. Chat Template LFM2.5 uses a ChatML-like format. See the Chat Template documentation for details. Example: <|startoftext|><|im_start|>system You are a helpful assistant trained by Liquid AI.<|im_end|> <|im_start|>user What is C. elegans?<|im_end|> <|im_start|>assistant <think> You can use tokenizer.apply_chat_template() to format your messages automatically. [!TIP] 💡 Note: Unlike LFM2-24B-A2B, LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a pure reasoning model that always thinks before it answers. It adds a <think> tag directly in the chat template when starting an assistant answer. Tool Use LFM2.5 supports function calling in four steps: Function definition: Provide the list of tools as a JSON object in the system prompt, or use tokenizer.apply_chat_template() with tools=.... Function call: By default, LFM2.5 writes Pythonic function calls (a Python list between <|tool_call_start|> and <|tool_call_end|> special tokens), as the assistant answer. You can override this behavior by asking the model to output JSON function calls in the system prompt. Function execution: Execute the call and return the result with the tool role. Final answer: LFM2.5 interprets the tool output and returns a plain-text answer addressing the original prompt. See the Tool Use documentation for the full guide. Example: <|startoftext|><|im_start|>system List of tools: [{"name": "get_candidate_status", "description": "Retrieves the current status of a candidate in the recruitment process", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"candidate_id": {"type": "string", "description": "Unique identifier for the candidate"}}, "required": ["candidate_id"]}}]<|im_end|> <|im_start|>user What is the current status of candidate ID 12345?<|im_end|> <|im_start|>assistant <|tool_call_start|>[get_candidate_status(candidate_id="12345")]<|tool_call_end|>Checking the current status of candidate ID 12345.<|im_end|> <|im_start|>tool [{"candidate_id": "12345", "status": "Interview Scheduled", "position": "Clinical Research Associate", "date": "2023-11-20"}]<|im_end|> <|im_start|>assistant The candidate with ID 12345 is currently in the "Interview Scheduled" stage for the position of Clinical Research Associate, with an interview date set for 2023-11-20.<|im_end|> Training LFM2.5-24B-A2B keeps the LFM2-24B-A2B architecture with two changes: the context window grows from 32K to 131K tokens, and the vocabulary doubles from 65K to 128K tokens through an in-place tokenizer expansion for better non-Latin tokenization. Pre-training: ~33T tokens, up from ~17T. Mid-training: 2T tokens at 32K context on curated, higher-quality data weighted toward reasoning, math, code, instruction following, and multilingual text, then 300B tokens of long-context data at 131K context. Tool calls and multi-turn trajectories appear in both phases. Post-training: supervised fine-tuning, teacher specialization, two multi-domain on-policy distillation stages (one non-agentic, one agentic), and agentic reinforcement learning inside popular agent harnesses (OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Pi, OpenCode), so the model learns their tools, system prompts, and interaction patterns. 🏃 Inference LFM2.5 is supported by many inference frameworks. See the Inference documentation for the full list. Name Description Docs Notebook Transformers Simple inference with direct access to model internals. Link vLLM High-throughput production deployments with GPU. Link SGLang High-throughput production deployments with GPU. Link — llama.cpp Cross-platform inference with CPU offloading. Link MLX Apple's machine learning framework optimized for Apple Silicon. Link — LM Studio Desktop application for running LLMs locally. Link — Quick start Get started with Transformers (compatible with transformers>=5.0.0): from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, TextStreamer model_id = "LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B" model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( model_id, device_map="auto", dtype="bfloat16", # attn_implementation="flash_attention_2" <- uncomment on compatible GPU ) tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id) streamer = TextStreamer(tokenizer, skip_prompt=True, skip_special_tokens=True) prompt = "What is C. elegans?" input_ids = tokenizer.apply_chat_template( [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors="pt", tokenize=True, )["input_ids"].to(model.device) output = model.generate( input_ids, do_sample=True, temperature=0.1, top_k=50, repetition_penalty=1.05, max_new_tokens=4096, streamer=streamer, ) Agentic Harnesses LFM2.5-24B-A2B supports tool calling for agentic workflows. Serve it locally with any OpenAI-compatible backend from the table above, then configure your agent harness to connect to it. For full setup instructions including installation and additional options, see our Agent Harnesses guide. Hermes Either use the interactive wizard or set it directly: hermes config set model.provider custom hermes config set model.base_url http://localhost:8080/v1 hermes config set model.default LFM2.5-24B-A2B hermes config set model.context_length 131072 hermes config set model.api_mode chat_completions hermes config set agent.tool_use_enforcement true OpenClaw Add to your config in `models.providers`: local: { baseUrl: "http://localhost:8080/v1", apiKey: "sk-local", api: "openai-completions", models: [{ id: "LFM2.5-24B-A2B", name: "LFM2.5-24B-A2B", contextWindow: 131072, maxTokens: 8192, cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 } }] } Pi Add to your config to `~/.pi/agent/models.json`: { "providers": { "local": { "baseUrl": "http://localhost:8080/v1", "api": "openai-completions", "apiKey": "local", "models": [{ "id": "LFM2.5-24B-A2B" }] } } } 🔧 Fine-Tuning We recommend fine-tuning LFM2.5 for your specific use case to achieve the best results. title: Federazione Semantica di Linked Open Data dell'Asia Orientale e Sud-Orientale, Ponti Cross-Dominio e Scoperta Automatica di Triadi Aperte Swanson ABC nell'Ipergrafo Rotta Aristeica Analisi Quantitativa di 11 Endpoint Live (#1240), 9 Vertici-Ponte Multi-Pilastro (#1242), Sensibilita' al Contesto Nullo Benjamini-Yekutieli e Demarcazione Fonologica (#1241- #1243)
abstract: La federazione di 11 infrastrutture Linked Open Data e Open Data dell'Asia Orientale e Sud-Orientale (5 nuovi endpoint W3C SPARQL 1.1 che portano la federazione da 24 a 29 nodi SPARQL attivi, affiancati da 6 distribuzioni RDF Turtle/JSON/XML API e dallo scarto documentato di 11 servizi non operativi) non genera di per sé alcuna scoperta automatica nel motore Swanson ABC fintanto che i nodi database e le sedi moderne restano isolati in quarantena (psca:swansonEligible=false) e i manufatti restano confinati a singoli articoli (78 triadi aperte complessive pre-ponti, 0 rigetti BY-FDR, score max 0.271811). Introducendo 9 vertici-ponte concettuali non geografici su 4 pilastri analitici (metallurgy_lia, linguistics_epigraphy, genetics_bio, material_cult_typology) e partizionando 4 iperarchi tematici di consenso (he728, he728_dongson_heger1, he728_kongorikishi_gandhara, he728_yayoi_bio_corridor) su 11.342 nodi @graph e 149.561 triple RDF SHACL-conformi, il numero di triadi aperte sale a 185 (Top-10 mediana +0.3295 vs baseline mono-dominio, MW p = 1.827e-04, Hedges g = 10.50). Dopo calibrazione su permutazioni, coda continua di Knijnenburg GPD e correzione conservativa Benjamini-Yekutieli (α = 0.05), emerge 1 associazione statisticamente significativa (Chang'an Q6501000 ↔ Linzi CHGIS hvd_85232, score = 0.73331, q_BY = 9.343e-05), mentre Cheonmachong (Gyeongju) ↔ Chang'an evidenzia un'istruttiva sensibilità al contesto nullo (q_BY = 0.01463 pre-#1243 vs 0.05921 post-#1243) e le piste Dian-Dong Son e Daisenryo Kofun rimangono ipotesi esplorative non significative a q_BY > 0.58. Parallelamente, gli audit #1241 e #1243 falsificano le convergenze grafiche tra Yaz (Tifinagh /z/), il carattere 木 (*C.mˤok > mù) su shuowen.space, 朱/銖 (*tjo/*djo > zhū [ʈʂu]) e i papiri di Cnosso. English Abstract The federation of 11 East and Southeast Asian Linked Open Data and Open Data infrastructures (5 new W3C SPARQL 1.1 endpoints expanding the federation from 24 to 29 active SPARQL nodes, alongside 6 RDF Turtle/JSON/XML API distributions and the documented exclusion of 11 non-operational services) yields no automatic discoveries in the Swanson ABC engine on its own, as long as database nodes and modern institutional locations remain quarantined (psca:swansonEligible=false) and artifacts remain confined to single publications (78 open triads pre-bridges, 0 BY-FDR rejections, max score 0.271811). By introducing 9 non-geographical conceptual bridge vertices across 4 analytical pillars (metallurgy_lia, linguistics_epigraphy, genetics_bio, material_cult_typology) and partitioning 4 thematic consensus hyperedges (he728, he728_dongson_heger1, he728_kongorikishi_gandhara, he728_yayoi_bio_corridor) across 11,342 @graph nodes and 149,561 SHACL-compliant RDF triples, open triads increase to 185 (Top-10 median +0.3295 vs single-domain baseline, MW p = 1.827e-04, Hedges g = 10.50). title: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake
abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces. We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. Fakes cover inner-face swapping, whole-frame video diffusion and voice conversion. MOZAIC has 137,745 clips from 15,014 source pairs and four tasks: T1 AV authenticity, T2 manipulation type, T3 identity verification and T4 explanation. We evaluate 12 AV multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), train four detectors and fine-tune MLLMs with LoRA. Overall, the best MLLM reaches only 35.6% on the four-way T1 and catches far more video-only fakes than voice-only fakes (43.6% vs 7.5%). Trained detectors reach 98.4% on T1, and LoRA fine-tuning raises explanation scores (OmniVinci 4.17 to 7.40, Qwen2.5-Omni 4.42 to 6.98), but the best T1 detector falls to 78.3% when the face-swap generator is held out of training, so generalization and explanation remain open. We release the dataset, the compact MOZAIC-SMALL split, the code and the prompts. https://vectorinstitute.github.io/mozaic/

title: Single-Transformer Latent Diffusion
abstract: Latent generative models typically rely on three separate networks: an encoder that tokenizes pixels, a generator that models the latent distribution, and a decoder that maps latents back to pixels. UNITE recently merged the first two into a single generative encoder trained in one stage, but its decoder remains a separate network. We ask whether this last network can be folded in too, so that one diffusion transformer encodes, generates, and decodes. Simply letting the shared backbone decode does not help. What makes it work is to cast all three modes as position-aligned sequence maps over one fully shared backbone, distinguished only by a mode token and the timestep. The resulting model, UNIFIED, is simple: one network trained from scratch in a single stage with only reconstruction and flow-matching losses, without adversarial losses or pretrained encoders (e.g., DINO). On ImageNet-1K 256x256 at matched parameters, UNIFIED improves gFID over UNITE at three sizes (~60M, ~115M, and ~215M) and reaches 2.08 with 215M parameters, the lowest among compared models under 250M parameters. On text-to-image generation, UNIFIED-B (218M) reaches a GenEval score of 0.87 at 512x512, exceeding single-stage pixel diffusion models with around one billion parameters. Full unification of latent diffusion is thus not merely feasible but beneficial.

title: NoHairCache: Calibrate-Once KV Cache Eviction with One Power-Law Exponent
abstract: The decay exponent α in KV-cache eviction is an intrinsic property of the model: calibrated once on a single corpus, it transfers directly across domains. Attention-based accumulation (H2O) and recency-based sliding windows (StreamingLLM) are two dominant eviction frameworks, often treated as unrelated, but we show that they are the two endpoints of a single power-law family: by scoring each token as s_i = A_i cdot (t-i)^{-α}, where A_i is cumulative attention and α controls the age penalty, H2O and StreamingLLM correspond to α=0 and αtoinfty, respectively (with StreamingLLM additionally hard-coding an attention-sink patch). The no-hair mechanism of xiang2026nohair bounds the admissible range of α, and the measured exponents agree: calibrating once on WikiText yields [0.556, 0.822] for a representative model (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct). The per-model ranges are consistent across five models (410M--1.5B) and independently match the optimal regions from perplexity sweeps. NoHairCache achieves the lowest perplexity across three datasets (WikiText, PG19, and arXiv) without per-dataset tuning, outperforming both H2O and StreamingLLM (p < 0.05 on all three datasets, with 0.06--0.10 PPL gains over StreamingLLM at budget 512). On downstream four-way multiple-choice QA, it matches or outperforms StreamingLLM across all nine (task, budget) cells, retaining 98.2% of full-cache accuracy on NarrativeQA at 25% retention versus 91.1% for StreamingLLM; per-cell McNemar tests are not significant, so QA is corroborating only. We release our calibration script and drop-in scorer upon publication.

title: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents
abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) built on vision-language models are increasingly entrusted with long-horizon tasks in live desktop, web, and mobile environments, where the screen keeps changing on its own. However, current CUAs lack real-time situational awareness: they perceive the environment through discrete snapshots, and the substantial inference latency of VLMs, compounded by highly dynamic interfaces, opens a perception-action gap in which the observed state frequently becomes stale before the corresponding action is executed. To bridge this gap, we present NightWatch, a plug-and-play framework that endows any CUA with continuous, temporally grounded perception without changing the agent's model, prompt, or action space. NightWatch couples the VLM agent with NightWatch-0.8B, a lightweight System-1 model that performs streaming monitoring of the interface state and keeps the agent synchronized with the evolving environment at low computational cost and latency, thereby grounding each decision in the current state rather than an outdated snapshot and reducing both stale actions and idle waiting while preserving task success. Experiments on desktop and dynamic web environments (OSWorld-Verified and DynaCU-Bench) show that NightWatch, driven by a watcher of only 0.8B parameters, reduces non-reasoning wall-clock time by 33% and wasted time by 53% on OSWorld while keeping task success on par, raises success on DynaCU-Bench from 39.5% to 44.2% with the large VLM agent, and is more efficient than passive-watching baselines such as AOI and PUSV under the same screenshot-only input, as well as a System-1 decision model more than 30times its size. Overall, NightWatch demonstrates that the timing of perception is as critical as its content, marking a step toward agents that maintain continuous awareness of their environment rather than perceiving it turn by turn.

title: Preregistration: Do LLM Pipeline Evaluations Notice Broken Preprocessing? A Mutation Analysis of Extraction Scorers
abstract: Preregistration (version 1.0) of a mutation study of LLM extraction pipelines on CUAD v1. Twenty-two mutation operators break stages outside the model (PDF reader, cleaner, chunker, prompt, parser, merge), and the study measures how often seven common scorers (exact match, SQuAD token F1, CUAD Jaccard, token-set, fuzzy, embedding similarity, LLM judge) fail to notice that the output changed, and whether three label-free stage checks catch what they miss. Posted before any study-set document was drawn or run. The zip holds the frozen code, the stratum file and the disclosed development dry run (5 contracts). sha256 of scorer-mutation-study_code_v1.0.zip: 5a5d251e6af2a82b458d0edc7dd2f424da46cd84f9de30779e2f6ddaf9960d4e

title: NAT: Scaling Causal Neural Action Tokenizers Across Embodiments
abstract: Action tokenizers let robot policies treat control as autoregressive next-token prediction. As these policies are trained on larger and more diverse datasets, they will need a universal tokenizer that can encode actions from many embodiments and data sources, including ones it has not seen. We study action tokenization at scale, training on 49k hours of action data from real-world robots, handheld grippers, simulation, and humans. We introduce Neural Action Tokenizer (NAT), a causal tokenizer whose decoder lets actions be executed as their tokens are generated. Across four simulation benchmarks, NAT outperforms FAST and prior neural action tokenizers when tokenizing unseen robot embodiments, and in vision-language-action models it outperforms FAST+ across four benchmarks and on a real robot when acting through its tokens. NAT tokens also close the performance gap to a flow-matching action head on some benchmarks while lowering the inference latency for first actions. Our experiments also find that robot data may not be necessary to learn an effective action space: a NAT trained only on human hand motion performs close to tokenizers trained on robot data.

title: CivilCADBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Understanding, Reconstructing, and Designing Civil Engineering Drawing Sets
abstract: Civil infrastructure is designed, built, and maintained through engineering drawing sets, yet preparing and revising them remains labour-intensive and calls for automation. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are promising candidates, but assessing them requires a benchmark grounded in real engineering practice. We introduce CivilCADBench, a benchmark for understanding, reconstructing, and designing civil engineering drawing sets, built from real infrastructure drawings and source CAD files containing over 250,000 CAD entities. Unlike parametric 3D CAD models, these drawings are dense, layered, and multi-sheet; and since prints are lossy projections with no pixel trace of layers, a file can print correctly yet remain wrongly organised. Grounded in real engineering practice, CivilCADBench exposes both the capabilities and the limitations of frontier models in professional civil engineering, laying a foundation for next-generation models and agentic systems for intelligent civil engineering.

title: Privacidad y seguridad en sistemas de aprendizaje federado: revisión de métodos y desafíos computacionales
abstract: Federated learning enables model training on distributed information without necessarily centralizing raw records. Nevertheless, parameter exchanges, participant coordination, and malicious behavior create threats that do not disappear when data remain at their source. This paper examines privacy and security safeguards in federated learning systems and their computational trade-offs. A structured narrative literature review was conducted through a targeted search of verifiable academic sources and thematic analysis of foundational studies, methodological contributions, and surveys. Findings distinguish inference and reconstruction attacks, model poisoning, backdoors, and server-related threats, and compare differential privacy, secure aggregation, robust optimization, and verification mechanisms. The reviewed literature suggests that no single method simultaneously guarantees confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Appropriate protection depends on the threat model, architecture, accuracy requirements, communication overhead, and computational constraints. Trustworthy deployment, therefore, requires complementary safeguards, explicit evaluation metrics, and reproducible tests tailored to each use case.

title: Guarding with Judgment: Learning to Intervene for Multimodal Safety
abstract: When visual context makes an ordinary request unsafe to answer as asked, a blanket refusal may leave the user's need unresolved. Choosing how to help requires distinguishing an established hazard from a condition that still needs verification, a distinction that binary safety labels leave unspecified. We formulate this decision through four actions: allow, warn, review, and refuse. To ground these decisions in verifiable evidence, we build a corpus of 20,126 training audits and the JudiBench benchmark, connecting each action to diagnostic judgments, source evidence, and controlled context changes. Our guard, JudiAct, separately states what the source establishes, what condition governs the help, and how the rules apply. It then checks these three brief review items against the original inputs to predict diagnostic labels and a handling action. Supervised training learns individual judgments while comparing label assignments across related cases. A second stage swaps one review item at a time, using the resulting audit feedback to refine review generation. On JudiBench, JudiAct improves request and answer Macro-F1 by more than 28 percentage points over its 4B backbone. Across nine public benchmarks, it outperforms state-of-the-art guards on the mean delivered-answer score in both pre-generation and post-generation settings, cutting MM-SafetyBench attack success from 40.78% to 25.30%.

title: Self-WSP: Can Language Models Improve Themselves Through Weight-Space Programming?
abstract: Frontier language models can now read and edit the weights of a neural network much like code and thereby improve a small model, an approach known as Weight-Space Programming (WSP). We further explore applying WSP to a language model itself, which we call Self-WSP. Specifically, Qwen3.5-0.8B reads its own weights, proposes an edit, and then continues with the edited weights as both problem solver and editor. We find many cases of genuine self-improvement. Self-edits can raise GSM8K accuracy from 11.8% to 62.2% and MATH500 accuracy from 7.0% to 32.2%, sometimes by changing only 16 parameters, and in some cases repeated self-editing keeps improving the model. A closer look, however, reveals that these gains lack interpretability. The model shows little understanding of the edits it makes, and WSP driven by random search sometimes performs comparably. Self-WSP thus holds promise as a path toward recursive self-improvement (RSI), but realizing this promise requires further exploration.

title: imr-anomaly-validation-ru: data and code for validating anomaly-detection algorithms on Russian regional infant mortality data, 2015–2023
abstract: Data and code for: Rusova V. S. Error Detection in Russian Infant Mortality Data: Validating Anomaly Detection Algorithms. Vestnik MIRBIS (version 2.0 of the article published as Vestnik MIRBIS, 2026, 1(45): 182–192, DOI 10.25634/MIRBIS.2026.1.20). The repository contains the regional panel of live births, infant deaths and the published infant mortality rate for 85 constituent entities of the Russian Federation, 2015–2023, reconciled cell by cell with the Rosstat operational bulletins included in data/raw; the computational scripts of all stages of the analytical protocol; machine-readable results of each stage, figures and execution logs; unit tests of the statistical methods; documentation of every analytical decision and a table linking each quantity reported in the article to the file in which it is computed. The analysis tests an anomaly-detection algorithm at three levels: its own computations, its operating characteristics on synthetic data with known anomalies and under admissible analytical specifications, and the limits of what is observable from aggregated data. A flag is a reason to check primary records, not evidence of an error; the absence of flags is not evidence that the data are free of distortion. Reproduce: pip install -r requirements.txt; python run_all.py (about one minute). Random numbers come from named streams derived from one seed (20260123), so runs are bit-for-bit repeatable. Licences: code under MIT (LICENSE); derived data, results and documentation under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA). Files in data/raw are official Rosstat publications reproduced unchanged.

title: Multimodal LLMs Know the Game but Assume the Real World
abstract: Multimodal large language models can state the rules of a video game, but do they apply them when they only see the game? We introduce RuleCraft, 1,240 image questions over 155 Minecraft rules with outcomes verified in the game engine, each asked in text, on the image with the game named, and on the bare image. Six widely used models know the rules and recognize the game, yet answer the bare image by real-world physics: naming the game raises their accuracy on rules where the game departs from reality by 8.2-19.8 points on a main set and by 33.8-52.7 on a hard stress-test set. Their errors pick the real-world outcome, the gap is largest where the game leaves a scene unchanged, and reasoning traces state the game's rule, then answer by reality. On the main set, naming the game mostly swaps the real-world default for the game's. The pattern holds with reasoning, recurs in two more games, and persists on questions the models themselves take to be about the game; one neutral sentence asking for the rules of the world shown recovers much of the gap. Evaluations that name the game measure knowledge of its rules, not world selection.

title: Overcoming Challenges in AI Adoption
abstract: Brad Pitt's Billy Beane was rebuilding the Oakland A's with a radical, data-driven philosophy in a room full of people who thought he was nuts. He had the numbers. He had the model. And for the first 40 games, the model looked completely wrong. The team lost. The scouts laughed. The old guard declared victory.

title: KMed-31B Technical Report
abstract: We present KMed-31B, a medical large language model post-trained from an open-weight model for on-premises deployment with limited hardware. Post-training a model for diverse medical tasks remains difficult, because improving one kind of task can lower performance on another. We attribute this to differences between tasks in expected output and available feedback. Medical question answering and diagnosis prediction have reference answers, whereas clinical inquiry has no single correct response and is judged with rubrics. We therefore divide medical training tasks into four categories by these two properties, train one specialist per category with a reward that its feedback supports, and integrate the specialists into a single student with Multi-teacher On-policy Delta Distillation (MOPD^2). For clinical inquiry, we build Synthetic Health Dialogue, a simulated corpus of consultations with lay users and clinicians whose patient cases span common clinical presentations in primary care. Relative to its base model, KMed-31B raises HealthBench Hard from 22.95 to 41.87 and HealthBench Professional from 37.92 to 50.20 in non-thinking mode, and from 23.80 to 51.48 and from 41.97 to 59.18 in thinking mode, while its scores on four multiple-choice medical benchmarks are maintained or slightly improved. KMed-31B has the highest unadjusted HealthBench Hard score among the compared models, including proprietary ones, and scores higher on HealthBench Professional than every open-weight model we compare, including models with more than ten times as many total parameters. Applied to another base model, Qwen3.8-27B, the same training recipe also raises both HealthBench scores. We describe the training recipe, data construction, and settings in detail so that institutions requiring on-premises deployment can develop medical models from open-weight foundations.

title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates
abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation. However, a multi-agent workflow that is fastest in one serving environment can lose its advantage in another, even when its models, prompts, and task remain fixed. This makes a benchmark result conditional on how the workflow is executed. We introduce MASSys, a benchmark for measuring this dependence in multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems. MASSys executes the same candidate-task pairs across serving substrates and load regimes, using five workload families spanning software repair, research synthesis, financial analysis, interactive control, and diagram generation. It records task quality alongside delivery, latency, cost, resource pressure, and failure evidence. In a controlled motivation diagnostic, the Star workflow falls from first to fourth in mean-latency rank under KV-cache pressure, while Chain rises from fourth to first. The substrate sweeps further show that increasing load creates long runtime tails and timeout pressure. In several task families, quality among evaluated outputs changes less than effective quality over submitted jobs: the system delivers fewer usable results even when the surviving outputs remain competitive. Tool and runtime traces reveal that these outcomes involve both model serving and non-model execution. Together, the results motivate evaluating MAS designs over explicit operating conditions and reporting which tasks are delivered, how well they are solved, and where execution breaks down.

title: Physical regime changes expose formula misuse in large language models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly employed for scientific computing across the Earth and environmental sciences, but problems in these fields often involve distinct physical regimes. LLMs may fail to recognize these regime-dependent constraints, applying formulas outside their domains of validity and producing plausible but physically incorrect results. We systematically investigate these failures through controlled experiments and assess whether post-training can improve regime-aware reasoning. Across 72 physical mechanisms, we find frontier LLMs frequently misapply formulas outside their regimes of validity, reducing accuracy by 13-57 percentage points. Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards enables Qwen3.5-9B to match DeepSeek V4 Flash (284B) on regime-dependent tasks, but its effectiveness is limited by the formulas available in the base model. Combining supervised fine-tuning on a few worked examples with reinforcement learning improves accuracy by 61 percentage points, while distillation from a teacher supplied with the correct formula raises accuracy from 0% to 71%.

title: RecallWorld: Episodic Memory for Persistent Embodied Video World Models
abstract: Video world models generate plausible novel views but often lack persistent memory, failing to preserve a place's geometry and appearance when an agent revisits a scene. A central challenge is how previous views should be effectively used for creating memory. Reconstructing them independently underutilizes geometric constraints between nearby views, while repeatedly reconstructing a growing history can propagate later prediction errors into earlier geometry. We introduce RecallWorld, a persistent embodied video world model that jointly reconstructs short multi-view episodes into Scenelets while keeping geometry independent across episodes. Starting from a single source image, camera-aware ray lifting places perspective and native fisheye images in a common world frame, retaining wide-field content for perspective generation. Each generated segment extends the Scenelet memory and conditions subsequent generation. Coverage-based retrieval selects complementary Scenelets from the full history, while target-view visibility is resolved geometrically before appearance fusion, providing consistent memory conditioning for guiding subsequent generation. Across four datasets, RecallWorld improves revisit PSNR over the strongest evaluated baseline by 2.6 dB on partial revisits and 3.9 dB on full cycles, demonstrating substantially stronger preservation of scene identity across exploration and return.

title: Seeing Right, Writing Wrong: Where Short Chain-of-Thought Breaks Spatial VQA
abstract: Asking a vision-language model (VLM) to think step by step often makes it worse at spatial questions, even though the image stays in context. We show that short chain-of-thought (CoT) turns a perception problem into a transcription problem. Once a VLM writes a spatial relation, its answer follows that sentence instead of the image, so whether CoT helps or hurts depends largely on whether the written relation is more accurate than answering directly. Studying 15 open VLMs (2B-38B) and six frontier closed models, we rule out token count, turn format, and visual forgetting in open models and trace the failure through three stages. First, writing re-weights visual cues, weakening a "lower is closer" shortcut in all 13 open models tested but also discarding valid cues, which produces false relations. Second, the written text takes over. With the model's own conclusion-removed rationale held fixed, swapping in an opposite-depth image moves the answer by 2-9 points on rendered twins (vs. up to 77 for direct answers) and by 3.0-3.4 points on average on natural photographs (vs. 20.5-69.6). Third, the concluding sentence can invert even a true relation, mainly on converse questions. Together, false relations and conclusion mis-mapping account for four in five CoT losses. Scale does not remove this bottleneck: Qwen3-VL-32B shows the same pattern. Frontier closed models are not hurt: they write relations as accurately as they answer, and three of six re-check the image after writing. The three queried with reasoning off lock in like open models, so re-grounding co-occurs with answer-turn reasoning; we identify answer-step re-grounding as the step open VLMs lack. In a single-model pilot, fine-tuning on fixed rationales with image-determined labels restores it on natural photographs. We open-sourced all our datasets and code at https://ming-zch.github.io/seeing-right-writing-wrong.

The three queried with reasoning off lock in like open models, so re-grounding co-occurs with answer-turn reasoning; we identify answer-step re-grounding as the step open VLMs lack. In a single-model pilot, fine-tuning on fixed rationales with image-determined labels restores it on natural photographs. We open-sourced all our datasets and code at https://ming-zch.github.io/seeing-right-writing-wrong.

title: Dual-Role Evaluation of Large Language Models in Cybersecurity: A Unified Framework for Offensive Generation and Defensive Intelligence
abstract: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) is reshaping cybersecurity by strengthening defensive capabilities while simultaneously enabling increasingly sophisticated offensive threats. Despite this dual-use nature, existing evaluation methodologies remain fragmented and commonly assess LLMs in isolation as either offensive or defensive systems. This work presents a unified dual-role evaluation framework that characterizes LLM behavior within a shared cybersecurity context through a multi-dimensional taxonomy encompassing role, capability, intent, and contextual use. The framework is empirically evaluated under a strictly single-turn setting (T = 1), in which each offensive input is independently assessed through one corresponding defensive response. The evaluation covers phishing detection, prompt injection, log analysis, malware reasoning, vulnerability exploitation, and incident response using malicious, benign, and ambiguous scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate strong overall detection performance, low error rates, and effective handling of dual-use and borderline cases through ambiguity-aware classification. The findings further reveal the difficulty of distinguishing malicious intent from structurally similar benign inputs, underscoring the importance of context-sensitive evaluation and uncertainty-aware decision making in cybersecurity applications. Overall, the study establishes a controlled and reproducible single-turn baseline for evaluating offensive inputs and defensive LLM responses across diverse cybersecurity tasks.

title: S-Mind: Internalizing Multi-View Geometry for Spatial Intelligence
abstract: Spatial intelligence, the ability to reason about 3D space from visual observations, becomes essential as multimodal large language models (MLLMs) move into the physical world. Beyond perceiving each view, it rests on two cornerstones of human cognition: fusing multiple views into one coherent 3D scene and mentally transforming that scene to new viewpoints as reasoning unfolds. Yet our spatial probes reveal that MLLMs largely lack both capabilities, even after spatial fine-tuning. We therefore present S-Mind, which internalizes multi-view geometry within the MLLM through a compact set of spatial tokens. It supervises these tokens to hold the fused 3D scene and re-emits them to re-express this scene from every viewpoint the reasoning adopts. Across four spatial benchmarks, S-Mind improves its Qwen3.5 backbones by up to 22.26 points and surpasses frontier general models such as GPT-6-Astra (+0.45), Kimi-K3.1-Pro (+1.97), and GLM-5.3-Flash (+7.80) in average accuracy. Moreover, the same probes confirm that it acquires both capabilities, reaching fusion and transformation accuracies of 65.11% and 82.17%, against at most 16.02% and 37.28% for the baselines. At inference, S-Mind also runs about 100x faster than a tool-based agent on the same backbone. Instilled through these spatial tokens during training, spatial capability becomes intrinsic to the backbone and persists even when the tokens are withheld, offering a promising path toward spatial intelligence in MLLMs.

title: Métodos de inteligencia artificial explicable: revisión de técnicas, aplicaciones y limitaciones
abstract: La inteligencia artificial explicable (XAI) agrupa procedimientos orientados a facilitar el examen de predicciones, representaciones y comportamientos de sistemas de aprendizaje automático. Este artículo analiza las principales familias de técnicas, sus ámbitos de aplicación y sus limitaciones, mediante una revisión narrativa estructurada de publicaciones académicas verificables. Se incorporan elementos de búsqueda y organización documental empleados en estudios bibliométricos, pero no estima indicadores de producción científica ni declara exhaustividad. Se clasifican las propuestas en modelos intrínsecamente interpretables, explicadores locales aproximados, atribuciones basadas en contribuciones, métodos de gradientes, explicaciones contrafactuales y enfoques globales. Los resultados muestran que cada familia responde a una pregunta explicativa distinta y exige criterios particulares de evaluación. LIME aproxima decisiones individuales, SHAP distribuye atribuciones entre variables bajo supuestos definidos, los gradientes caracterizan sensibilidades en redes diferenciables y los contrafactuales identifican modificaciones capaces de alterar resultados. La utilidad de estos recursos se encuentra limitada por inestabilidad, dependencia de distribuciones de referencia, problemas de fidelidad, restricciones causales y divergencias entre evaluación técnica y comprensión humana. Se concluye que una explicación no debe equipararse con validación, causalidad, equidad o confiabilidad del modelo.

title: LoopSeek: Decoupling System One Search from System Two Answering for Long Video Understanding
abstract: Long video question answering requires finding relevant evidence before reasoning over it. With a limited frame budget, single-pass frame selection can miss critical evidence, while adaptive search often relies on repeated text generation to decide where to look. We introduce LoopSeek, a framework that decouples evidence search from answer generation through a division of labor between a non-thinking System I and a generative System II. Our key insight is that search can be expressed as a sequence of small, typed decisions, allowing System I to find the evidence that System II needs. Four System I role agents navigate a tree of video windows and coordinate through probability outputs to select frames, assess evidence, and revise the search without generating text. To align search with System II, System I learns from annotated evidence on questions that System II answers correctly only from that evidence, and the verifier's evidence estimates steer the search without calling System II, which stays frozen and answers once from the selected frames. On five long-video benchmarks, with a frozen Qwen3-VL-8B reading 32 frames, LoopSeek improves average accuracy from 53.5 to 63.9 over the uniform baseline and takes 32--80\% less GPU time per question than agentic methods.

title: Distilling Visual Agents from Limited Interaction Experience
abstract: How much interaction experience is needed to distill a capable visual agent? We study learning from few tasks and recorded interaction histories. Our framework selects representative trajectories using skill-context coverage and ordered visual-decision similarity. On-policy distillation (OPD) learns through fresh interaction on selected tasks or fresh student responses at fixed histories. Across Navigation, Sokoban, and spatial mapping, even one online training task supports transfer to other tasks. Four fixed trajectories raise a 4B student's success from 49.17% to 82.08% on standard Navigation and from 60.16% to 85.55% on Sokoban, recovering over 90% of the measured gap to a 27B teacher on these panels. On an independent Navigation panel, replay improves success from 45.83% to 76.67%, retaining 91.36% of the same-task online gain without new interaction during optimization. Training repetitions, matched supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and a 9B extension further support the value of compact experience.

title: A Near Neighbour Is Not a Native Feature: What Nearest-Neighbour Novelty Detection Owes to the Space It Measures In, Why the Case For and Against Pretrained Features Turns on Benchmark and Baseline More Than on Where the Features Came From, and the Comparison That Would Separate Scoring Rule From Representation
abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Life of Research A novelty detector is trained on normal data and asked to flag whatever is unlike it. Since 2020 two positions have competed over how such a detector should be built. One holds that the decisive ingredient is a feature space borrowed from a network pretrained on a large external corpus, after which a nearest-neighbour distance is enough, and that self-supervised or reconstruction-based detectors trained only on the normal data are outclassed. The other holds that detectors trained in-domain, such as autoencoders whose novelty score combines the reconstructions of an input's nearest latent neighbours with the distance to them, are competitive without any pretrained network and transfer to domains, such as radio-telescope spectrograms, that look nothing like natural photographs. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that the two positions are answering a question neither benchmark design isolates. A published comparison of two detectors almost always changes at least three things at once: the space in which distance is measured, the rule that turns distance into a score, and the kind of novelty the benchmark plants, while a fourth factor, the evaluation (metric, baseline implementation, hyperparameter selection), decides which of the three gets the credit. On one industrial benchmark, published image-level results for detectors that all use ImageNet features and a distance or density score range from 75.0 to 99.1 AUROC, a spread several times larger than the 3.3-point margin by which the nearest-latent-neighbour autoencoder beats its own re-implementation of the pretrained baseline. On one natural-image benchmark, supervised ImageNet features with a simple density score are reported at 80.0, 86.2 and 92.5 AUROC by three groups. Off the pretraining distribution the verdict flips with the dataset: in one seven-dataset medical study a plain autoencoder beats frozen ImageNet features on two datasets and loses by up to 36 points elsewhere, and an autoencoder whose residual is measured in pretrained feature space beats both on most. The paper consolidates nineteen published results in a table and a figure, states a procedure for crediting a novelty-detection gain to a representation's origin rather than to the scoring rule or the evaluation, and names the studies that would settle what remains open.

title: EvoViM: Recursively Self-Evolving Visual Agents for Exploration with Deferred Queries
abstract: Multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents have shown promising capabilities in task-oriented environments. However, they still struggle when queries are deferred until after exploration, requiring them to retain visual evidence before knowing which details will matter. We introduce EvoViM, a recursively self-evolving framework in which a frozen multimodal model turns its own interaction experience into one visual program for memory and skills. The program retains images and computes directly on pixels, and its operations decide how this evidence is used in each task. During memory evolution, the same model traces failures in its visual trajectories to the operations that lost or misused evidence and revises them. It also rewrites the notes and analysis tools that guide later revisions, which then build on earlier findings and skip changes that have already failed. We evaluate EvoViM with three multimodal models on six tasks covering visual matching, spatial recall, and sequential decision-making, including three tasks with deferred queries. Across the six tasks, EvoViM improves the average score over AutoMem, the strongest baseline in the main comparison, by 31.3-47.6 points on held-out episodes. Programs written once from the initial environment instructions perform substantially worse, highlighting the value of interaction experience in shaping how visual evidence is retained and used. Code and dataset are available at https://evovim.github.io/.

title: LLM 的甜区:可定义、可表述、有数据、可验证的问题(数字生命·讨论稿)
abstract: 讨论稿。提出一个判断框架:LLM 的"甜区" = 同时满足四个条件的问题:①存在确切的函数;②现有数学工具能准确表述它;③现实中或模拟中存在大量数据;④结果可验证(或有可靠检查器)。四条件齐备时逼近器发挥最大作用;缺一个就要用别的手段补(形式化、模拟器、实验、人工验证),能力打折。给出边界情形(半甜区:数据少/验证弱/表述难/无函数)与例子表(数学、代码、棋、肥皂泡/极小曲面、天气、开放写作、价值判断、罕见天文事件逐条对照四条件)。与能力极限的关系:甜区不是没有极限,而是"四道门里最宽的地"(熵/预算/验证/可计算性仍生效)。给出工程判据:拿到新任务按四问检查(可定义?可表述?有数据?可验证?),任一不能就找替代路径。边界:定性框架、无量化阈值、未做系统实验检验;条件间不独立;可能存在反例;与已有讨论(压缩即智能、验证器引导、缩放律)有重叠但未做文献对照。

title: X-AQA: Unifying Action Quality Assessment with Multimodal Large Language Models and Multi-Domain Learning
abstract: Action Quality Assessment (AQA) aims to evaluate the quality of human actions, yet existing methods are predominantly developed and evaluated on individual datasets with different task formulations and assessment criteria. We introduce X-AQA, the first unified training and evaluation framework for general-purpose AQA with multimodal large language models (MLLMs). We construct X-AQA-40K, a training corpus comprising 40,163 samples from 22 data sources across four domains: competitive sports, fitness exercises, rehabilitation, and general skills. We convert heterogeneous annotations into a unified question-answering format, incorporating dataset-specific annotation guidelines and official scoring rules when available. Using this corpus, we fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B to develop a single MLLM capable of handling diverse AQA tasks. We further establish X-AQA-Bench, which evaluates both in-distribution (ID) performance on datasets represented during training and out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization on four held-out datasets. The resulting model outperforms all evaluated open-source MLLMs on X-AQA-Bench and achieves competitive performance relative to proprietary MLLMs. Ablation studies further demonstrate that multi-domain joint training and explicitly providing assessment criteria in prompts both improve OOD generalization. X-AQA establishes a unified foundation for advancing general-purpose AQA across diverse real-world domains. Data and models are released at https://huggingface.co/collections/Kelly0510/x-aqa{here}.

title: Weight-Space Backdoors in Open-Weight LLMs: Cross-Architecture Attacks and Blind Model Forensics
abstract: Open-weight language models are vulnerable to trigger-conditioned behaviors introduced through sparse post-training weight modifications, creating supply-chain risks beyond conventional provenance checks. We present Neural Sentinel, a cross-architecture study of gradient-guided backdoor insertion and model forensics spanning 18 checkpoints across 14 architecture families (124M-31.3B parameters), including state-space and recurrent models. On Phi-2, modifying approximately 0.0002% of parameters induced an exact short-marker output after 300 steps (332 seconds), with mean next-token KL divergence of 1.5 times 10^{-5} and 100% top-1 agreement over evaluated positions of eight fixed reference prompts. Separate experiments produced structured tool-call-formatted outputs without establishing downstream execution. We identify three procedure-dependent response regimes -- Gradient-Permeable, Scale-Threshold, and Gradient-Fragmented -- and evaluate PPO-based weight-space exploration, which showed no statistically significant advantage over random search. For defense, Neural Sentinel combines weight-difference analysis, trigger discovery, activation probing, and contextual output inspection. In a 22-artifact development cohort, its reference-optional scanner classified 4/5 backdoored artifacts as BACKDOORED; the remaining positive and all 17 clean artifacts were SUSPICIOUS. These findings establish the feasibility of sparse conditional-output insertion and evidence-producing forensic triage, while identifying limitations in behavioral-drift assessment and clean-model admission.

title: VG3R: Video Generation Model for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction
abstract: Video generation models are widely used as 3D priors for novel view synthesis and 3D scene generation. Fine-tuned for perception, generation models also excel at dense prediction such as depth estimation. However, methods that apply video generation models to 3D reconstruction either predict depth without cameras or generate geometry and estimate cameras through many iterative denoising steps, which makes them slower. In this paper, we present VG3R, which turns a pretrained video generation model into a feed-forward 3D reconstruction model. Our key observation is that such a model already captures the depth and camera motion of a video, but not in the form required for reconstruction. We introduce two components: clip-level shift prediction, which corrects depth distortion caused by the unknown shift in decoded inverse depth, and a multi-layer camera head, which predicts per-frame cameras parameters by combining features across transformer blocks. Using Wan2.1 as its video backbone, VG3R reconstructs a scene and estimate the camera of every frame without iterative denoising. It achieves the lowest ATE and reconstruction errors among methods built on video generation models, runs about 4 and 14 times faster than Aether and Geo4D. VG3R also demonstrates competitive depth estimation and 3D reconstruction performance compared with geometry foundation models. Project page: https://github.com/KTH-RPL/VG3R

title: Open Vision Banana: An Open Framework for Unified Visual Perception through Generation in RGB Space
abstract: Vision Banana showed that a closed image generator, instruction-tuned to paint perception outputs as RGB images, becomes a generalist vision model. Does this carry over to open generators, and if not, what fails? We answer with Open Vision Banana (OVB), an open framework that adapts the 7B diffusion generator of Qwen-Image-2.1 into one instruction-driven model for metric depth, semantic, instance, and referring segmentation, using a single shared low-rank adapter and public data. Each task is a task contract whose RGB encoder, instruction, and decoder share one specification and are checked before training. Studying 42 externally evaluated checkpoints from two 100k-update runs, six exact weight-space merges, and eight controlled shorter runs, we find that the gap to the closed system is specific and measurable. Geometry is learned early while absolute scale is not: median-aligned NYUv2 δ_1 stays at 0.89--0.93 throughout training as unaligned δ_1 wanders between 0.11 and 0.50. The scale is not committed by a single sample: a ten-seed ensemble lifts unaligned δ_1 from 0.348 to 0.516 without retraining. Depth and 2D segmentation compete for the shared adapter, and weight merging moves along this trade-off without escaping it. Finally, lower validation flow loss comes with lower Cityscapes accuracy (Spearman ρapprox-0.9 between loss reduction and mIoU), so the loss cannot select checkpoints. We release code, contracts, training data, and all evaluation outputs.

title: Relative periodic orbits of a free spinning loop
abstract: A closed elastic string with no external forces can hold any shape while its material moves steadily along the curve (a steady axial motion), because its tension and the force needed to turn the material around a bend are both proportional to the curvature. I compute the periodic motions that grow from the simplest of these motions, the spinning ring, by Newton's method on a chain of masses. They include rotating waves that turn at twice the rotation rate of the material, standing "flappers" with two to five lobes, and period-doubled and period-tripled orbits. The chain only approximates the string. The orbits and their strong instabilities change little with more masses and are properties of the continuous string. Most weak instabilities change with the number of masses and are artifacts of approximating the string by a finite chain. The saddle flapper of a loop stretched 30% beyond its natural length is neutrally stable at small heights and unstable at large ones. Near a stretch of 1/12 the saddle flapper resonates with the breathing of the ring. Below that stretch the flapper slows as it grows and above it the flapper speeds up, and near the resonance two families of saddle flappers overlap. An unstable saddle flapper trades energy back and forth with an in-plane oval, and at large amplitude the energy spreads to the shortest waves of the chain. For Keller's linear string, whose tension is proportional to the stretched length, every motion is periodic, and every knot carries an exactly periodic flapper. For a Hookean string the curvature of a knot couples a ripple to stretching waves that travel at a different speed, and in the simulations a ripple on a sliding knot does not return to its starting shape. Whether a Hookean knot carries any periodic flapper is open.

title: Range-Only Dynamic Output Feedback Controller for Safe and Secure Target Circumnavigation
abstract: The safety and security of robotic systems are paramount when navigating hostile targets. This paper addresses the problem of circumnavigating an unknown target by a unicycle robot while ensuring it maintains a desired safe distance and remains within the sensing region around the target throughout its motion. The proposed controller design is based on a composite Lyapunov framework consisting of: (i) a quadratic Lyapunov function characterizing the target-circumnavigation objective, and (ii) a barrier Lyapunov function-based potential term enforcing the prescribed safety and sensing constraints. A notable feature of the proposed approach is that it relies exclusively on local range measurements between the robot and the target, achieved through a dynamic output-feedback controller that treats the range as the only measurable output. Using Lyapunov-based stability analysis together with an equivalent autonomous reformulation of the closed-loop dynamics, we establish asymptotic stability of the desired equilibrium while guaranteeing satisfaction of the prescribed safety and sensing constraints under the proposed controllers. Restrictive bounds on the post-design signals are also derived, and numerical simulations are presented to validate the proposed approach.

title: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction
abstract: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extends residual connections to multiple streams and stabilizes residual propagation by constraining stream-mixing residual matrices to the Birkhoff polytope, the set of doubly stochastic matrices. In this work, we investigate how to effectively mix residual streams within the Birkhoff polytope. We reveal a mixing trade-off: when under-mixed residual matrices stay close to the vertices of the Birkhoff polytope, hyper-connections will degenerate into a set of nearly independent streams; when over-mixed residual matrices are concentrated around the uniform barycenter of the polytope, streams will become less distinguishable from each other. We theoretically validate our findings by bounding the cumulative residual mixing, stream difference and gradient difference of mixing coefficients across layers. Motivated by these findings, we propose Contraction for Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (cmHC), an exact doubly stochastic method which geometrically contracts the Birkhoff polytope toward its interior. This contraction mitigates under-mixing by forcing the residual matrices to explore deeper into the polytope, with a provable stream mixing bound and no new parameterization. Moreover, we apply a moderate contraction at the shallow layers to prevent over-mixing, enabling stable gradient propagation on extremely large-scale model pretraining. Extensive experiments across dense and mixture-of-experts models at various parameter scales demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of cmHC. We also develop fused operators for cmHC on Ascend NPUs, reducing hyper-connection execution latency by up to 44.8%.

title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
abstract: We study high-probability linear regression in the infinite variance regime, wherecthe regression noise has only a finite conditional $α$-moment $ν$ for some unknown $α\in(1,2)$, and the covariates may only have finite moments up to a given order (e.g., 4th moment). We give a black-box reduction that converts finite-variance regression procedures into weak-moment procedures. The reduction is based on empirical residual pruning and is agnostic to the moment exponent, the noise scale, the covariance, and the design moment. Under a finite fourth-moment condition on the covariates, any finite-variance subroutine attaining the sub-Gaussian rate yields the following when the number of samples $n$ is above a suitably defined threshold: Without knowing $α$ or $ν$, we have with probability at least $1-δ$ that $ \|\widehatθ-θ^*\|_Σ \lesssim_α ν^{1/α} \big(\frac{d+\log(1/δ)}{n}\big)^{\frac{α-1}α}, $ where $d$ is the dimension, $Σ$ is the covariate covariance matrix, and $\|v\|_Σ:=(v^\topΣv)^{1/2}$. We further prove a matching minimax lower bound that holds under the same conditions. The reduction is computationally efficient whenever the finite-variance subroutine is. We also obtain a distribution-free prediction guarantee under a bounded raw $α$-moment assumption on the response, and give an analogous $α$-agnostic reduction for mean estimation.

title: A Methodologically Rigorous Benchmark of Linear Regression,RNN, and LSTM for S&P 500 Forecasting:Identifying Sources of Performance Inflation in Financial DeepLearning
abstract: This study examines one-day-ahead forecasting of the S&P 500 closing level using a 2006-2025 dataset that includes fundamental price data, macroeconomic indicators, and engineered technical features. We benchmark three model families, namely linear regression, vanilla recurrent neural networks (RNN), and long short-term memory networks (LSTM), within a unified preprocessing and chronological evaluation pipeline. A central contribution of this work is a methodological audit of common practices in the deep-learning-for-stock-prediction literature. We identify three sources of result inflation that frequently appear in published methodologies: wavelet-denoised evaluation targets, the absence of a naive persistence baseline, and best-of-N replicate reporting. We then re-evaluate all model families under a corrected protocol that controls for each. Performance is reported using root mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, and the Pearson correlation coefficient, averaged across N = 30 independent replicates per configuration. We compare models on accuracy, stability across replicates, and architectural depth sensitivity, using the naive persistence forecast (predicting today's close as tomorrow's close) as a primary baseline against which all candidate models must demonstrate improvement.

title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents
abstract: Language-model agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) face three runtime verification gaps: (i) action fabrication, where post-tool prose narrates side effects that failed, timed out, or never ran; (ii) provenance collapse, where unverified model prose or web text enters durable memory alongside executed tool outputs; and (iii) syndicated echo amplification, where mirrored web pages satisfy multi-source corroboration from one origin. Existing MCP firewalls inspect wire calls before execution, while LLM-judge guardrails require multi-gigabyte VRAM without binding prose to receipts. We present epistemic-guard (v0.5.2), an open-source Python library and out-of-process stdio MCP receipt proxy (15 modules, 0 MiB GPU VRAM). epistemic-guard isolates Ed25519 signing keys out of process, writes RFC 6962 Merkle logs with AER-1 receipt translation, checks post-turn prose on CPU with SHA-256-verified OpenVINO INT8 encoders (4 models, 279.48 MB total; 82.67 MB on the supervision path), gates SQLite writes across 7 provenance domains, and collapses verbatim and lightly edited wire-syndicated RAG mirrors. On conformance suites, epistemic-guard rejects 100.0% of tampered receipts (200 Merkle leaves), passes 58/58 official AER-1 ingestion vectors and 50/50 reference-verified AER-1 exports, verifies 100.0% of 40 fault-injected wire calls and 100 concurrent appends with 0 key leaks, and blocks 100.0% of 100 unauthorized memory writes. Across $N=250$ frozen-benchmark traces, epistemic-guard reaches 93.2% accuracy at 17.9 ms warm median CPU latency (8.62 ms single-clause; 921.8 ms cold-start load), beating 12B-14B GPU judges by 6.4-6.8 points ($p=0.0259$, $p=0.0095$) at 4.26-4.5$\times$ lower latency; on $N=60$ live mcp-proxy traces, it catches 96.15% of hazards at 76.67% accuracy (38.24% FPR; $+18.34$ points over Stage-1-only, $p=0.001$) in 9.16 ms p50.

title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
abstract: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models. MemOnce is based on two core designs: (a) Memory encoder-decoder: it caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory representations and dynamically decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers; (b) Memory sparse attention: for each continual input, MemOnce adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations, with the sparse indices computed only once across layers. Coupling these two designs enables efficient on-the-fly memory loading and KV cache decoding, drastically reducing the GPU memory footprint and achieving linear-time complexity. We conduct extensive experiments to show that MemOnce outperforms Transformers and other architectures across varying model sizes, context lengths, and training paradigms (pretraining and post-training adaptation). In particular, adapting Qwen3.5-4B with MemOnce reduces memory state cache by 1313$\times$ and prefill latency by 6.9$\times$ at 1M context, and improves throughput by 3.5$\times$ and overall memory performance by +5.77%. Finally, MemOnce generalizes zero-shot to downstream representation tasks, achieving competitive results against specialized models.
